title: One-Pan Broccoli Spaghetti with Anchovy Butter
changes_from_base: A one-pan version: the spaghetti cooks in a measured amount of water with broccoli and anchovy butter, so its starch thickens the sauce. No tomatoes.
summary: Spaghetti cooked in one pan with broccoli, garlic and melted anchovy butter, so the pasta starch turns everything into a glossy sauce.
equipment: large deep frying pan with high sides (30 cm)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prep the broccoli
steps.text: Peel the stalk, then cut the stalk and thick stems into 1 cm pieces and put them in the pan with the garlic. Chop the florets into spoon-sized pieces and keep them separate; stalks need longer to soften.

steps.title: Anchovy butter
steps.text: Add the butter and anchovies to the pan and set over medium-high heat. Cook 2-3 min, mashing the anchovies into the butter, until they melt away and the stalks have softened.

steps.title: Cook it all in one pan
steps.text: Add the dry spaghetti, the florets, salt, chilli and the water and bring to a boil. Cook 8-12 min, turning everything with tongs every minute or so, until the pasta is al dente and the liquid has thickened into a glossy sauce. Add a splash more water if it dries out before the pasta is done; the starch the spaghetti releases is what makes the sauce.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Eat straight away with grated Parmesan.

tips: Keep tossing; spaghetti cooked in little water sticks if left alone.
Do not skip the stalks, as they add sweetness and bulk.
The anchovies melt away, leaving savoury depth rather than a fishy taste.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours for up to 2 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot (74 °C).
